checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is ModExp gas computed before memory allocation?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm is a consensus client (OffchainLabs/prysm @ 238d5c07df). It does not implement the EVM or any EVM precompiles. ModExp is an EVM precompile (address 0x05) implemented exclusively in execution clients (go-ethereum, Nethermind, Reth, Besu). Exhaustive grep search for 'modexp', 'mod_exp', 'ModExp', 'precompile', 'Precompile' across all Go files in the target_workspace returned zero results.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: No ModExp code exists in OffchainLabs/prysm. The abstract state domain for this property is empty within this repository. Prysm communicates with the execution layer via Engine API (engine_newPayload, engine_forkchoiceUpdated) and treats execution payloads as opaque objects validated by the EL. No state anomalies can be identified because the code under test does not exist in this audit target.
phase1.cache_analysis: Not applicable - no EVM execution engine or precompile cache in Prysm.

phase2.symbolic_execution: No symbolic execution paths exist from any Prysm entry point to ModExp gas computation or memory allocation. The execution order (parse lengths -> compute gas -> check gas -> allocate) is entirely enforced by execution clients and is opaque to Prysm.

phase2_5.attack_surface: None. ModExp execution happens in the EL, which communicates with Prysm only through Engine API. Prysm does not inspect precompile gas accounting.

phase3.invariant_analysis: The invariant 'ModExp gas is computed before memory allocation' (PROP-W3B12-47) is an execution-layer invariant enforced by EVM implementations. No such invariant exists or can be proven/disproven in Prysm. Prysm's only participation is accepting VALID/INVALID response from engine_newPayload.

phase3_5.scope_reasoning: Prysm is a consensus client. ModExp (EIP-2565/EIP-7883) is an EVM precompile implemented exclusively in execution clients. Exhaustive code search confirms zero ModExp-related code in OffchainLabs/prysm. This property is completely outside the scope of this audit target.
phase3_5.recommendation: Redirect this check to execution client audits (go-ethereum, Reth, Nethermind, Besu).

audit_items.reasoning_summary: OffchainLabs/prysm is a consensus layer client that does not implement the EVM. ModExp is an execution-layer precompile. No relevant code exists in this repository. Property is definitively out of scope.

checklist_item.title: Do specific EIP-7883 test vectors produce expected gas costs?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm is a consensus client. EIP-7883 modifies the ModExp precompile gas formula (removal of division by 3, minimum 500 gas). This is an execution-layer EIP. Grep for '7883', 'modexp', 'ModExp', 'precompile' across all .go files in target_workspace: zero results. Matches found in api/client/builder/types_test.go and beacon-chain/rpc/eth/shared/testing/json.go were coincidental substring matches in transaction hex strings, not EIP-7883 code.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: No EIP-7883 gas formula code exists in Prysm. The property asks whether specific (base_length, exp_length, mod_length, exponent_value) tuples produce the correct gas cost. Prysm has no gas cost tables for ModExp, no BigInt exponentiation code, and no test vector framework for EVM precompiles. The abstract domain is empty.

phase2.symbolic_execution: No paths exist. The test procedure (execute ModExp at specific inputs, observe gas cost) cannot be applied to this codebase. EIP-7883 test vector compliance is a property of the EVM implementation in execution clients.

phase2_5.attack_surface: EIP-7883 gas costs are visible to users as transaction costs on the execution layer. No attack surface exists at the Prysm consensus layer for this property.

phase3.invariant_analysis: The formal invariant 'test vector X produces gas cost Y for EIP-7883' is not a consensus-layer concern. Prysm's consensus responsibility terminates at verifying engine_newPayload returns VALID. Internal gas accounting is opaque to Prysm. No guard or proof mechanism exists in this codebase.

phase3_5.scope_reasoning: EIP-7883 ModExp gas formula compliance is an execution-layer property. OffchainLabs/prysm is a consensus client. Comprehensive code search confirms no ModExp gas computation code exists anywhere in this repository. This item is definitively out of scope for this audit target.
phase3_5.recommendation: Redirect to execution client audits (go-ethereum, Reth, Nethermind, Besu).

audit_items.reasoning_summary: EIP-7883 test vector compliance is an execution-layer property. Prysm has no ModExp gas computation code. Property is definitively out of scope.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7825 gas cap activated only at Fusaka fork block?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm (consensus client) participates in gas limit management for block proposals and builder bids. The expectedGasLimit function validates that a proposed gas limit conforms to the EIP-1559 adjustment algorithm. No EIP-7825 cap constant (16777216, 0x1000000) exists anywhere in the codebase. Fork naming: Prysm uses 'Fulu' (not 'Fusaka') for this upgrade cycle. FuluForkEpoch = math.MaxUint64 on mainnet (not yet scheduled). The function has no upper-bound cap: it only enforces the parentGasLimit +/- parentGasLimit/1024-1 adjustment.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The abstract domain for GasLimit in Prysm's gas limit handling is: any uint64 value adjusted by the EIP-1559 parent gas limit adjustment formula (max change of parentGasLimit/1024-1 per block). There is NO upper bound cap of 16777216 (EIP-7825) enforced anywhere. The FuluForkEpoch = math.MaxUint64 means no fork-conditioned cap logic exists. When the fork is eventually scheduled, the gap between what Prysm enforces (unbounded gas limit adjustment) and what EIP-7825 requires (hard cap at 16777216) will create a vulnerability.
state_anomalies: EIP-7825 gas cap (16777216) is ABSENT from the Prysm codebase
expectedGasLimit() has no upper bound - only implements EIP-1559 adjustment arithmetic
FuluForkEpoch = math.MaxUint64: fork not yet scheduled, but implementation gap exists
No fork-epoch-conditioned gas limit cap check in any code path
phase1.cache_analysis: The PayloadIDCache at beacon-chain/rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/validator/proposer_execution_payload.go does not cache gas limit validation results. Each block proposal recomputes expectedGasLimit. No cache staleness risk for this property.
phase1.concurrency_analysis: No concurrency issues identified in gas limit computation. The function is stateless and deterministic.

phase2.symbolic_execution:
Symbolic analysis of expectedGasLimit:
  INPUT: parentGasLimit=P (any uint64), proposerGasLimit=R (validator-controlled)
  maxGasLimitDiff = P/1024 - 1 (if P > 1024)
  CASE R > P: result = P + min(R-P, maxGasLimitDiff)
  CASE R <= P: result = P - min(P-R, maxGasLimitDiff)
  NO CONSTRAINT: result is never capped at 16777216

Attack path: Validator registers GasLimit = math.MaxUint64. Each block, Prysm computes expectedGasLimit ratcheting up by parentGasLimit/1024-1. After sufficient blocks, GasLimit > 16777216. When EIP-7825 is live in EL, EL returns INVALID for engine_newPayload, causing missed slot.

Chain split attack: If some CL clients implement EIP-7825 cap in consensus-layer gas limit validation and Prysm does not, they will accept/reject different sets of blocks at fork activation, causing a consensus split.

attack_scenarios.scenario: Missed slot via gas limit inflation
attack_scenarios.description: Attacker-controlled validator registers GasLimit = 2^64-1. Prysm's expectedGasLimit ratchets GasLimit upward by ~1/1024 per block. At Fulu fork epoch, if gas limit has been driven above 16777216 and EL enforces EIP-7825, engine_newPayload returns INVALID, causing missed slot.
attack_scenarios.attacker_control: Validator registration gas limit parameter (--suggested-gas-limit flag)
preconditions: Gas limit has been inflated above 16777216 pre-fork

attack_scenarios.description: If CL clients implementing EIP-7825 cap check reject blocks with GasLimit > 16777216 after fork, while Prysm (lacking the check) accepts them, the network may split.
attack_scenarios.attacker_control: Block proposal timing around fork epoch; gradual gas limit inflation
preconditions: Other CL clients implement consensus-layer EIP-7825 cap

timing_dependencies: Attack requires Fulu fork to be scheduled (currently FuluForkEpoch = MaxUint64 - dormant)
Gas limit inflation requires multiple blocks to ratchet above 16777216

entry_points: Validator registration via --suggested-gas-limit flag flowing through getPayloadHeaderFromBuilder
phase2_5.attack_surface: Any validator operator can control their registered GasLimit. The expectedGasLimit function is called during builder bid validation. No upper bound cap prevents gas limit inflation beyond EIP-7825's 16777216 threshold.

phase3.invariant_analysis:
INVARIANT (required by EIP-7825): After Fulu fork epoch, gasLimit <= 16777216.
STATUS: NOT ENFORCED in Prysm.

The guard at proposer_bellatrix.go:262-264 validates: computed = expectedGasLimit(parent, proposed); if computed != header.GasLimit() -> reject. This guard ensures the EIP-1559 adjustment arithmetic is correct, but does NOT check computed <= 16777216. A block with gasLimit = 17000000 (above EIP-7825 cap) after fork epoch would pass this guard.

No fork-conditioned cap check exists anywhere in the codebase. The Fulu fork epoch gate in engine_client.go uses FuluForkEpoch to select payload types for Engine API, but does not inject a gas limit cap.

guards_identified.enforces: EIP-1559 gas limit adjustment bounds (+/-1/1024 per block)

edge_cases: Blocks with GasLimit between 16777217 and ~30M (historical mainnet values) at fork activation
The spec requires gas limit to be 'wound down' to cap at fork activation - no such logic exists in Prysm
Builder bids with GasLimit above cap would pass Prysm's validation but fail EL validation

phase3_5.scope_reasoning: This is a real implementation gap: EIP-7825 gas cap enforcement is absent from Prysm's consensus-layer gas limit validation. The expectedGasLimit function (proposer_bellatrix.go:446-462) implements only the EIP-1559 adjustment arithmetic without any absolute upper bound. When the Fulu fork is scheduled, Prysm proposers could create payloads with GasLimit > 16777216 that the EL rejects (engine_newPayload returns INVALID), causing missed slots. Additionally, if other CL clients implement the cap check and Prysm does not, a consensus split occurs. The vulnerability is currently dormant (FuluForkEpoch = MaxUint64) but is a concrete pre-existing gap.
phase3_5.recommendation: Add EIP-7825 cap enforcement in expectedGasLimit (proposer_bellatrix.go). After computing the adjusted gas limit, if the current epoch >= FuluForkEpoch and result > 16777216, cap at 16777216. Also add a validation check in block processing to reject payloads with GasLimit > 16777216 post-fork. File: beacon-chain/rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/validator/proposer_bellatrix.go, function expectedGasLimit (lines 446-462).

audit_items.reasoning_summary: EIP-7825 gas cap (16777216) is completely absent from Prysm's expectedGasLimit function. When Fulu fork is scheduled, validators with inflated GasLimit could produce blocks rejected by the EL, causing missed slots and potential consensus splits. Currently dormant due to FuluForkEpoch = math.MaxUint64, but a real, concrete implementation gap.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7883 ModExp formula activated only at Fusaka fork block?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm is a consensus client (OffchainLabs/prysm). It does not implement the EVM or any EVM precompiles including ModExp. EIP-7883 modifies the ModExp precompile gas formula in the EVM - this is an execution-layer change. Prysm uses 'Fulu' as the fork name for this upgrade cycle (FuluForkEpoch = math.MaxUint64 on mainnet). The fork name 'Fusaka' does not appear anywhere in this codebase. Prysm signals fork activation to the EL via Engine API payload types gated on FuluForkEpoch. No ModExp code found anywhere in target_workspace.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: No EIP-7883 code, no ModExp precompile, and no 'Fusaka' fork name exists in Prysm. The abstract state domain for this property is empty in this codebase. The EIP-7883 formula change (removing division by 3, adding minimum 500 gas floor) is an execution-layer change. Prysm's fork epoch gating (FuluForkEpoch in engine_client.go) correctly signals the fork boundary to the EL via Engine API. No state anomalies in Prysm for this property.
state_anomalies: NOTE: The audit checklist uses 'Fusaka' fork name but Prysm uses 'Fulu' - this is a naming inconsistency in the checklist, not a code defect in Prysm
phase1.concurrency_analysis: The fork epoch transition handling in engine_client.go correctly gates Fulu-specific Engine API call variants on epoch >= FuluForkEpoch. No concurrency issues observed in fork activation logic.

phase2.symbolic_execution: The only Prysm code path relevant to EIP-7883 activation is the Engine API version selection. When epoch >= FuluForkEpoch, Prysm uses Fulu-specific payload types, signaling to the EL to activate Fulu-era EIPs. This is the correct mechanism. Prysm does not and cannot verify that the EL correctly applied EIP-7883 to specific transactions - that is by design.

entry_points: Engine API fork selection in engine_client.go (gated on FuluForkEpoch)
phase2_5.attack_surface: Fork epoch is a configuration parameter, not attacker-controllable. No attack surface for EIP-7883 activation timing exists within Prysm's scope.

phase3.invariant_analysis: The invariant 'EIP-7883 ModExp formula activated only at Fusaka fork block' is correctly delegated to the execution layer in Prysm's architecture. Prysm's responsibility is to signal the correct fork epoch to the EL via Engine API (using FuluForkEpoch as the gate), which it does. The EL independently enforces the new gas formula only after the fork epoch. This is the correct trust boundary delineation.

guards_identified.enforces: Fulu-era Engine API payload type selection (signaling fork to EL)
guards_identified.does_not_enforce: EL-internal ModExp gas formula (by design - EL's responsibility)

phase3_5.scope_reasoning: EIP-7883 ModExp gas formula is an EVM precompile change implemented exclusively in execution clients. Prysm correctly delegates fork signaling to the EL through the Engine API using the FuluForkEpoch configuration. No ModExp code exists in Prysm. The fork name 'Fusaka' in the checklist vs 'Fulu' in Prysm is a naming inconsistency in the audit checklist, not a code defect. This property is definitively out of scope for this audit target.
phase3_5.recommendation: No action needed in Prysm. Redirect EIP-7883 ModExp fork activation checks to execution client audits (go-ethereum, Reth, Nethermind, Besu).

audit_items.reasoning_summary: EIP-7883 is an EVM precompile change implemented in execution clients. Prysm (consensus client) correctly delegates fork activation signaling to the EL via Engine API gated on FuluForkEpoch. No ModExp code exists in Prysm. Property is definitively out of scope.
